doc.title: Jason Marsalis — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Opening, setting and the evening's gig
summary: Brown introduces the Smithsonian NEA interview in New Orleans on November 7, 2010. Marsalis is dressed for a gig at Preservation Hall with clarinetist Tommy Sancton.

story.theme_name: Starting the tape: names, dates and places
story.community_name: Opening the interview: introductions, date and place

blocks.x: Funding for the Smithsonian Jazz Oral History Program NEA Jazz Master interview was provided by the National Endowment for the Arts.
Interviewer: Anthony Brown with recording engineer Ken Kimery Description: Transcript, 47 pp.

Today is November 7th, 2010, and we are at 1304 St. Claude in New Orleans, Louisiana. We are conducting the Smithsonian NEA Jazz Oral History Interview with Jason Marsalis. Good afternoon, Jason. How you feeling?
I’m feeling very good. How about you?
I see you’re dressed for a gig. So you got to run to a gig right after we’re done here, I see.
I’ll have some time. But I thought that I would get ready right now and be presentable. I’ll be performing a little later on this evening.
I think it’s a pianist. No, it’s a clarinetist named Tommy Sancton. I think it’s going to be his show.
Let’s start from the beginning. If you could state your full name and your date of birth and place of birth.
